record.original_question: How can active representation learning integrate representation learning with sequential decision making in partially observable environments where data must be acquired by interacting with a complex physical system through measurements, so that exploration skills and exploration policies are derived from actionable representations while those representations also improve future data acquisition?

evidence.quote: In this work, we introduce Active Representation Learning, a class of problems that intertwines exploration and representation learning within partially observable environments.

However, such an active approach to representation learning requires integrating aspects of sequential decision making with representation learning concepts. This raises the question: How can we integrate representation learning and sequential decision making?

Active representation learning (ARL) is a set of problems that involves deriving Exploration Skills (ES), informed by Actionable Representations (AR), to learn a suitable exploration policy π, see Figure a.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a partially observable environment modeled as a controlled stochastic process in which, at each time step t, an agent selects an action a_t from an action space A, the environment's hidden state x_t evolves according to an unknown transition kernel P(x_{t+1} | x_t, a_t), and the agent receives an observation o_t drawn from an unknown emission kernel O(o_t | x_t, a_t). No reward signal is provided; the agent's data is the trajectory (a_1, o_1, a_2, o_2, ...) generated by interaction.

Define an actionable representation as a measurable map φ: H → Z from the space H of interaction histories to a representation space Z, such that φ supports downstream decision-making (i.e., it is sufficient for predicting future observations and for planning). Define an exploration skill as a parameterized policy σ_θ(a | φ(h)) that selects actions based on the current representation, and an exploration policy π as a (possibly hierarchical) composition of exploration skills whose purpose is to acquire informative data for learning φ.

Formulate and solve the following problem: design an algorithm that simultaneously
(i) learns an actionable representation φ from interaction data alone (no external rewards or labels),
(ii) derives a set of exploration skills and an exploration policy π from φ, and
(iii) uses π to acquire new interaction data which, in turn, improves φ,
in such a way that the joint procedure converges, with provable guarantees on sample complexity and on the quality of the learned representation, to a representation that is sufficient for an arbitrary downstream task in the same partially observable environment.

In particular, specify (a) a precise objective functional coupling representation quality and exploration efficacy, (b) conditions on the environment (e.g., on the transition and emission kernels) under which the coupled objective is tractable, and (c) finite-sample bounds relating the number of interaction steps to the suboptimality of the learned representation and exploration policy.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open programmatic challenge: integrating representation learning with sequential decision-making for partially observable environments through actionable representations and exploration skills. While related strands (unsupervised RL, exploration via empowerment/intrinsic motivation, representation learning in POMDPs) have produced partial advances, no general algorithmic framework with provable guarantees solving the full coupled problem has been established. The status appears open.

status_evidence.title: Open Problem: Active Representation Learning
status_evidence.snippet: We introduce Active Representation Learning, a class of problems that intertwines exploration and representation learning within partially observable environments.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly framed as an open problem class without a known general solution.
